quarterly_data.signal: Full OBERON and TITANIA Phase III results for tozorakimab (anti-IL-33, 300mg every four weeks) in COPD, presented at the ERS Congress 2026 and published in the New England Journal of Medicine: moderate and severe exacerbations were reduced versus placebo on inhaled standard of care by 29% (OBERON) and 34% (TITANIA) in the primary population of former smokers, and by 30% (OBERON) and 29% (TITANIA) in the overall population of current and former smokers. In the pooled analysis, patients with a baseline blood eosinophil count below 150 achieved a 23% reduction, those at or above 150 a 34% reduction and those at or above 300 a 43% reduction; an integrated analysis also showed a reduction in mucus plug score. The trials randomised 2,306 patients over 52 weeks; the only adverse drug reaction was injection-site reaction. The US FDA accepted the Biologics License Application for Priority Review as an add-on maintenance treatment for adults with COPD, with the PDUFA date anticipated during the first quarter of 2027 following use of a Priority Review voucher; tozorakimab is also under regulatory review for COPD in the EU and China, and is in a Phase II trial in severe asthma and a Phase III trial in severe viral lower respiratory tract disease (FDA Fast Track Designation for COPD since December 2024). The company calls it the first biologic to show statistically significant efficacy on exacerbations in a broad COPD population (company claim).
